teaser: A blueprint for products with no server and no database of yours: static files, the user's own AI key and storage, and agents to build them.
core_idea: A product can be built, in phase one, as a folder of HTML, CSS and JavaScript with native web components and vendored libraries, running offline and anywhere, while the user brings the AI key, the storage and the passkey, so the company is never in the line of a request; the gaps are on the providers' side, capped per-user keys and paying the app that brings the customer.

quotes.text: Nothing in that loop passes through the company that built the studio.
Serverless is taken, and it means something else

figures.caption: The usual SaaS and the no-server product. On the left, the company sits in the line of every request, with its servers, its database, its AI key and its bill. On the right, the product is a folder of files, and the user brings the AI key, the storage and the passkey.
One folder, served from anywhere: a laptop with no network, a simple server, a container, GitHub Pages, Cloudflare or any cloud, a function that returns files, or a customer's isolated network.

The infographic studio as eight steps, none through the company that built it. Six work today; a cap on the user's own key works with a catch; and getting paid for bringing the provider a customer is missing.
How a founder builds it: agent sessions and synthetic users around one repository, a dev site and a main site, and the team hired in order, explorers, then villagers, then town planners.
The no-server studio in its vault: an invented bakery's quarter as a poster, drawn in the browser, in simulation mode.
The business plan in the vault: three businesses in one blueprint, packages and prices as hypotheses, go-to-market, ninety days, a calculator, risks as acceptances and open questions.
